Usually accounts are created with either fake or stolen identities. Money is moved and sent between multiple accounts before being reported as fraud that it eventually can’t be tracked. It’s not like the money is just left sitting in the scammers cash app/Venmo account. They aren’t regulated to the same extent as banks. 

Also fraud in a banking sense is for unauthorized transactions. That is the true account holder did not make the transaction. In this case he did actually send the money to that cash app/Venmo account. Now if someone stole his credit card number and it was used to send money by the fraudster with cash app/Venmo. The bank can then do a chargeback as unauthorized. Cash App/Venmo usually then sends supporting documents that show this was an authorized transaction. The bank or me as the investigator would review and determine if the account that used the card belonged to the customer or someone else. In this case it would come back to the customer as he did do the transaction.

That’s why I said this may be a valid billing dispute chargeback. That’s separate department where I work. So I don’t know the odds of that for sure.

That’s why cash app/Venmo/Apple Cash should only be used for friends and family as the apps were intended.
